newsitem.title: USA: Oravax says HNK20 trials did not meet goal.
newsitem.headline: Oravax says HNK20 trials did not meet goal.

text.p: OraVax Inc said Wednesday that initial review of Phase III trial results of its HNK20 nosedrop showed the primary goal of the tests was not met as there was no statistically significant reduction in the hospitalization of subjects included in the study.
HNK20 is a monoclonal antibody for the prevention of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
The study was designed to determine how effective the nosedrop was in infants who are premature and have brochopulmonary dysplasia that put them at risk of lower respiratory tract infection.
Lance Gordon, president and chief executive officer of OraVax, told Reuters that based on the results, "we are not filing a license application later this year."
He said OraVax will carefully review its options for the RSV program.
"Although this trial demonstrated some positive trends, it did not replicate in human infants the high level of protection HNK20 demonstrated in non-human primate studies," he said.
"The analysis of the results is far from over," he added.
OraVax expects to conclude the analysys, consider alternative dosing levels or schedules, and review the status of next-generation candidates for the RSV program, he added.
"We continue to believe in the need for an effective, easy-to-administer product for prevention of RSV-associated viral pneumonia in high-risk infants," he said.

In the study, 614 infants at 26 centers in Australia, New Zealand, Argentina and South Africa received either 2.5 milligrams of HNK20 or a placebo. The drug was administered once daily for up to 120 days. The study was conducted between May and November 1996, the usual transmission season of respiratory syncytial virus in the Southrern Hemisphere's winter months.
The initial review of results showed there was a 24 percent decrease in lower respiratory tract infections, with 53 cases occurring in the placebo group and 40 in those administered with HNK20.
Some 35 of the 308 subjects in the placebo group, or 11.4 percent, were hospitalized, compared with 31 of the 306 subjects treated with the nosedrop, or 10.1 percent.
"These results do not represent a statistically significant reduction in hospitalization rates, which was the study's primary endpoint," OraVax said.
